findings.evidence: Fig 7.6 caption: "... so it fits on a single 48–80 GB GPU (e.g. an H100), not on the 24 GB or 32 GB devices above."
findings.issue: Caption/figure mismatch. The figure shows only 1×H100 (80 GB), 2×H100 (160 GB), and 8×H100 (640 GB) capacity lines; no 24 GB or 32 GB device appears in the figure. "48–80 GB" and "24 GB or 32 GB devices above" refer to text elsewhere, not to anything shown in the figure.
findings.fix_instruction: Either add the 24 GB and 32 GB device lines to the figure, or rewrite the caption to reference the text (e.g., "fits a single 80 GB H100, unlike the 24 GB consumer device discussed in §7.3.1") rather than "above".

findings.evidence: Table 7-2 — Inference residency vs. fine-tuning residency contrast for the canonical 80-layer, hidden-8192, full-MHA 70B reference model.
findings.issue: Table 7-2 is titled 'Inference residency vs. fine-tuning residency' but contains six rows, four of which are inference-side variants (inference FP16, inference FP16 grads, QLoRA, inference with FP8 KV). Only two rows are fine-tuning. The title does not describe the table's actual content, and the column header 'scenario' hides that 'inference with FP8 KV' is an inference row, not a fine-tuning row. A reader scanning for the fine-tuning figure can mistake rows and mis-attribute the ~152 GB FP8-KV residency to the training regime.
findings.fix_instruction: Retitle the table to match its content, e.g. 'Memory floors by scenario: inference variants and fine-tuning variants (canonical 80-layer, hidden-8192, full-MHA 70B)', or split into two tables (Table 7-2a inference, Table 7-2b training/adaptation). Add a 'regime' column (Inference / Fine-tuning / Adapt) so the row classes are explicit.

findings.evidence: fine-tuning (weights + gradients + optimizer) ... Adam: ~16 B/param ... ~1,120 GB
findings.issue: Table 7-2's ~1,120 GB fine-tuning figure is arithmetic-inconsistent with the book's own components given on p. 157 (§7.6): 'the same model that serves in ~165 GB demands ~1,120 GB under full Adam fine-tuning (weights 140 GB + gradients 140 GB + Adam m/v/master states 840 GB)'. 140 + 140 + 840 = 1,120 GB, but that implies the optimizer/master term is 840 GB = 12 B/param, which contradicts the table's own 'Adam: ~16 B/param' label (16 × 70B = 1,120 GB for weights+grads+optimizer ALONE, i.e. 1,400 GB if weights 140 + grads 140 are counted on top of 1,120 GB of optimizer states). The table's 16 B/param row and the prose's 840 GB optimizer term cannot both be true.
findings.fix_instruction: Reconcile the two figures to one accounting: either (a) state 'weights + grads + Adam m/v/master = 16 B/param total' and drop the additive 140 + 140 + 840 phrasing, giving ~1,120 GB as the floor, or (b) keep the additive decomposition and correct the B/param label to ~12 B/param for the optimizer term. State explicitly in one place which convention the 16 B/param figure uses.

findings.evidence: figure 7.3: Quantization choices and execution paths: quantization (calibration) method, numerical representation, packed tensors and checkpoint container describe different parts of a deployment, and loading still requires a kernel-required runtime layout with compatible dispatch.
findings.issue: Figure 7.3 is titled 'Quantization choices are not execution guarantees' in the rendered page and the caption's first clause restates the title ('Quantization choices and execution paths'), then the caption body shifts to a different claim ('describe different parts of a deployment'). Two titles for one figure — the in-figure heading 'Quantization choices are not execution guarantees' and the caption's 'Quantization choices and execution paths' — with different predicates. The List of Figures (p. 9) uses the caption form ('Quantization choices and execution paths'), so the rendered figure and the apparatus disagree.
findings.fix_instruction: Align the figure's internal heading and the caption/list entry to one title, e.g. 'Figure 7.3: Quantization choices are not execution guarantees: method, representation, container and dispatch are separate decisions.' Update the List of Figures to match.

findings.evidence: KV budget per rank: 436 ÷ 8 = ~54.5 GB • per-request KV per rank: 24.9 ÷ 8 = ~3.1 GB (tensor-parallel attention shards each request's KV across the 8 ranks)
findings.issue: The per-rank figures are computed by dividing the aggregate host KV budget (436 GB) and the aggregate per-request KV (24.9 GB) by 8, on the assumption that a request's KV is sharded evenly across all 8 ranks. For the canonical full-MHA geometry (64 query heads, 64 KV heads, head_dim 128) with TP=8, the KV heads per rank are 64/8 = 8, so an even shard holds — but for the GQA variant the KV heads are 8, and 8/8 = 1 per rank, which changes the per-rank KV bytes per request from 3.1 GB to 24.9/8 = 3.1 GB only coincidentally (GQA-8 with TP=8 would place all 8 KV heads on one rank in some layouts, or 1 per rank in others). The note is presented as a settled per-rank budget without stating the head-partition assumption, even though Ch. 7 elsewhere insists that 'per-rank fit' must be validated separately and that TP shards attention heads, not the hidden dim.
findings.fix_instruction: State the partition assumption in the technical note: 'per-rank KV assumes an even 64 KV heads ÷ 8 ranks = 8 heads per rank for the canonical full-MHA geometry; a GQA-8 model at TP=8 places 1 KV head per rank, and a layout that replicates KV heads changes the per-rank figure.' Mark the per-rank numbers as conditional on the partition plan.

findings.evidence: figure 7.7: The concurrency budget: 140 GB weights + ~64 GB runtime/NCCL leaves ~436 GB of KV budget ... C ≈ 17.5 concurrent (floor 17, not 18; the band's height is the KV budget and the arithmetic 436 ÷ 24.9 carries the 17-slot decomposition), and FP8 (~12.45 GB/request) roughly raises it to ~35.0.
findings.issue: Arithmetic check of the FP8 figure: 436 GB ÷ 12.45 GB = 35.02 → ~35.0 ✓. But the chapter's own per-request FP16 KV is quoted in two forms — '24.9 GB' (rounded, from 24.90368 GB) in Fig 7.7 and the byte-accurate '24.9037 GB' in the technical note — while the FP8 figure '12.45 GB' is the exact halving of the rounded 24.9 (24.90368/2 = 12.45184). Using the rounded 24.9 gives 436/12.45 = 35.02; using byte-accurate values 436/12.45184 = 35.01. Both round to 35, so no numerical defect; the defect is that Fig 7.7's caption says the arithmetic '436 ÷ 24.9 carries the 17-slot decomposition' while the adjacent technical note insists the byte-accurate quotient is 17.51 and 'the conservative integer 'requests that fit' floor is 17, not 18'. Two precisions for the same divisor are used in the same section without a stated rule for which figure to quote.
findings.fix_instruction: State the rounding rule once at the head of §7.3: 'Per-request KV is quoted as 24.9 GB (byte-accurate 24.90368 GB); quotients are computed on the byte-accurate value and then floored to whole slots.' Then have Fig 7.7 and the technical note both cite 24.90368 GB as the divisor.

findings.evidence: figure 7.8: Memory Tetris: how the 8×H100 host's 640 GB aggregate pool fills at 9.5K / 32K / 128K ... (light rules = 80 GB rank boundaries) ... 9.5K context = 229 GB used ... 32K context = 288 GB used ... 128K context = 539 GB used
findings.issue: Re-derivation of the figure's totals: 140 + 64 + 24.9 = 228.9 ≈ 229 ✓; 140 + 64 + 83.9 = 287.9 ≈ 288 ✓; 140 + 64 + 335.5 = 539.5 ≈ 539 (truncation) — the third is presented as '539' while the pattern of the first two is rounding-to-nearest (229, 288). 539.5 rounds to 540 or 539 depending on convention, and the figure prints 539. The figure's own caption states 'Bar heights are to scale (GB)', so a 0.5 GB discrepancy against a 640 GB axis is immaterial to the drawing — but the label arithmetic is inconsistent with the other two labels' rounding convention, and the caption also asserts '436/335 = 1.30 → 1 at 128K' where 436/335.5 = 1.300 exactly (using the rounded 335 GB gives 1.302).
findings.fix_instruction: Use one rounding rule for the three labels: 229 / 288 / 540 GB (140 + 64 + 335.5 = 539.5, rounded up to 540 to reflect the bound), or print 539.5 GB. Use the byte-accurate 335.46 GB (128,000 × 2,621,440 B) in the quotient 436 ÷ 335.46 = 1.30 → 1 so the caption's arithmetic matches the label.

findings.evidence: Table 7-3 — Frontier 2026 KV-scheme claims (first-party reported, not independently reprofiled). model reported KV claim source DeepSeek-V4 hybrid CSA+HCA: KV cache ~10% (Pro) / ~7% (Flash) of DeepSeek-V3.2 at 1M-token context [1P: arXiv 2606.19348]
findings.issue: The source column gives arXiv identifiers without a resolvable title, and — more importantly — the arXiv IDs are dated identifiers that sit outside the book's own evidence-cutoff discipline: arXiv 2606.19348 implies June 2026 and arXiv 2607.24653 implies July 2026, both inside the 2026-08-30 cutoff, but the table gives no access date, no paper title, and no version, while the References chapter (p. 497) is the book's declared location for 'a stable identifier' per source. The book's stated rule (Preface p. 18: 'each is cited with a stable identifier in the References chapter') is only partially honoured here: the inline table cites bare arXiv IDs without the version qualifier the Preface requires for dated claims. The DeepSeek-V4 row also states a comparison against 'DeepSeek-V3.2' with no source for the V3.2 baseline, so the ~10%/~7% ratios are not reproducible from the printed material.
findings.fix_instruction: Add to each row's source cell the paper title, arXiv version, and access date, and cross-reference the References entry number ([S#]) as the book does elsewhere ('[S3][1P][FACT]'). Add the source for the DeepSeek-V3.2 baseline figure so the ~10%/~7% ratios are reproducible, or mark the ratios as the vendor's stated comparison without a second-party baseline.

findings.evidence: Fine-tuning is a different memory regime than inference. The same model that serves in ~165 GB demands ~1,120 GB under full Adam fine-tuning (weights 140 GB + gradients 140 GB + Adam m/v/master states 840 GB) — roughly 1.75× the 8×H100 host.
findings.issue: Recomputation of the components: 70B × 2 B = 140 GB (weights) ✓; gradients at FP16 = 140 GB ✓; the remaining 1,120 − 280 = 840 GB for 'Adam m/v/master' = 12 B/param (FP32 master copy 4 B + m 4 B + v 4 B = 12 B) ✓ — so the prose's decomposition is internally consistent and the 840 GB is correct. But it contradicts Table 7-2's own 'Adam: ~16 B/param (FP16 weights + gradients + FP32 master copy + Adam m + v)' label, which counts weights and gradients inside the 16 B/param and would therefore imply 1,120 GB as the *whole* floor (not 840 GB of optimizer). The same page therefore carries 16 B/param ≈ 1,120 GB total and 16 B/param ≈ 840 GB optimizer-only — a 12-vs-16 B/param contradiction for one row's label.
findings.fix_instruction: Choose one convention and use it in both places. If the label is 'Adam optimizer states alone: ~12 B/param (FP32 master + m + v) = ~840 GB', then the prose's 'weights 140 + gradients 140 + 840 = 1,120 GB' and the table's '~16 B/param total' both hold and the table's parenthetical must drop 'FP16 weights + gradients +' from the 16 B/param description. Add one clarifying line to Table 7-2: 'the 16 B/param label counts the full weights+grads+Adam state set; the optimizer term alone is ~12 B/param.'
